import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a bar plot to visualize the survival rate by passenger class and sex
# 'survived' column contains 0s and 1s, so the mean directly represents the survival rate.
sns.barplot(x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', data=df, palette='viridis', errorbar='sd')

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Titanic Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis tick labels for better readability
plt.xticks(ticks=[0, 1, 2], labels=['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'], fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend for 'sex'
plt.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize='12')

# Improve layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
